as_told: NASA studied the world's languages and found that Sanskrit is the best, or the only unambiguous, language for computers and artificial intelligence. NASA scientists are said to be using or learning Sanskrit for this reason.
lesson: Sanskrit is uniquely suited to computers and artificial intelligence.
what_happened: In the Spring 1985 issue of AI Magazine (vol. 6, no. 1, pp. 32-39), Rick Briggs, whose address is given as RIACS, NASA Ames Research Center, published 'Knowledge Representation in Sanskrit and Artificial Intelligence'. He argued that the method of paraphrase used by the old Indian grammarians of Shastric Sanskrit gives the same kind of analysis as the semantic nets used in AI, that 'there is at least one language, Sanskrit' that served both as a living language and as an unambiguous one, and that 'a natural language can serve as an artificial language also'. The article is one researcher's paper in the magazine of the American Association for Artificial Intelligence. It does not rank Sanskrit against other languages for computing or say it is the best language for AI. NASA's only link shown in the paper is the author's address.
false_part: The paper does not say Sanskrit is the best language for AI, and nothing in it presents its argument as a finding of NASA; its only NASA link is the author's address at NASA Ames.
